findings.claim: Step numbering mismatch in Task 8. The README numbers the plain-mock work as step 3 (line 143) and uses step 2 for the check-yourself question (line 142), but the test TODO says "TODO Task 8 step 2" (line 81) and both new failure messages start "step 2:" (lines 93 and 96). A learner who reads a failing "step 2: build a BookingController ..." message and goes to README step 2 lands on the question, not the instruction.
findings.recommendation: Renumber one side so the TODO and both messages name the same step as the README (step 3), or fold the check-yourself question out of the numbered list.

findings.claim: The location check is a substring match on Location.toString(): contains("BookingController.create("). Critic mutant on the overlay (loop 4): a test-local record named FakeBookingController, declared inside WebLayerTest, whose create forwards to the plain mock, used in place of the real controller: all 12 tests pass, because the recorded frame is bookings.WebLayerTest$FakeBookingController.create(WebLayerTest.java:N). The README line 144 claim that the checks fail unless the call comes from a BookingController the learner built is therefore slightly too strong. The format itself is sound at the pinned version: Spring Boot 4.1.2 manages mockito-core 5.23.0, whose StackWalker-based LocationImpl printed "-> at bookings.BookingController.create(BookingController.java:36)" in a critic run (the inline mock frame is skipped), but Location.toString() is documented only as a human-readable location, not a stable format. Contrived: it takes more effort than the intended edit and is not a plausible misconception.

evidence.section: Location.toString(): Human readable location in the source code

findings.recommendation: Anchor the match on the package-qualified frame (for example contains(" bookings.BookingController.create(")), or soften README line 144 to say the check looks for a call made from inside a create method of a BookingController.

findings.claim: verifyNoMoreInteractions can be satisfied without any verify call. Critic mutant on the overlay (loop 4): in both Task 8 tests, stub create with an any() matcher before the call and call Mockito.ignoreStubs(mock) in place of verify: all 12 tests pass. Mockito documents that ignoreStubs marks all stubbed invocations as verified. This predates the delta for task8VerifiesTheCreateCall (line 75) and carries into the new test (line 94), so README lines 140 and 144 ("any call on the mock is unverified" / "every call on it is verified") overclaim slightly. Contrived: ignoreStubs is an advanced API a learner at this point is unlikely to reach for.

evidence.section: ignoreStubs(Object...): all stubbed methods of given mocks are marked verified

findings.recommendation: Optionally add a shipped assertion that the mock carries no stubbing of create (mockingDetails(mock).getStubbings() has no create stubbing), or accept the residual and leave the README wording as is.
